# Edmund S. Muskie Internship Program
The Edmund S. Muskie Internship Program is a professional exchange initiative supported by the United States Department of State, established by Congress in fiscal year 1992 (Pub. L. 102–138, Sec. 227) and named following the Freedom Support Act of 1992 (Pub. L. 102–511, Sec. 801). Originally administered by the International Research & Exchanges Board and various American Councils, the program was restructured and relaunched by Cultural Vistas in 2015 with a renewed format and scope. Its primary objective is to provide summer internship placements, career training, and financial support to Eurasian scholars and graduate students studying in the United States.
The program aims to foster international understanding through direct engagement with American culture and professional environments. While the text notes that the program was previously administered by specific councils, it currently operates under Cultural Vistas. The initiative serves as a mechanism to bring Eurasian students to the U.S. for immersive experiences, aligning with the broader goals of the Muskie legacy in diplomacy and education, although specific current selection criteria or application processes for the 2015 reformed version are not detailed in the provided text beyond its administrative history.
